problem: Modular/learned ObjectNav methods generalize poorly, while zero-shot VLM value-map methods (e.g. VLFM) degrade when semantic cues in the scene are weak; no single module handles both dense and sparse semantic-cue regimes.
motivation: Semantic cue strength varies across environments; local VLM cues are reliable in semantically rich views, whereas a learned prediction from the global semantic map is more useful when the view has few cues. Adaptively balancing the two should give both generalization and scene adaptability, and false target detections also need to be suppressed.
key_idea: Fuse a U-Net target-location predictor on the semantic map (converted to a distance map) with a SmolVLM value map, weighting them per step by a Semantic Cue Intensity (SCI) computed from the fraction of confident semantic pixels in the FOV, to choose frontiers.
insight: Ablation (Table 2) shows both modules help and are complementary: removing the target prediction module (TPM) drops SR/SPL to 35.6/15.3, the largest drop, and removing the value map (VM) drops it to 36.2/16.4. Both single-target and multi-object semantic/confidence maps also contribute (removing MOL gives 35.5/16.5, removing STL gives 36.6/16.8). Gains over VLFM are small (+2.0 SR, +0.2 SPL), so SPL improvement is marginal.
method: Multi-scale Fusion Map Builder: maintains single-target and multi-object semantic maps with matching confidence maps (keep the higher confidence, else average), plus obstacle, explored and frontier maps built from RGB-D, GroundingDINO detection and Mobile-SAM segmentation.

VLM Value Map: SmolVLM-500M scores the current RGB against the target prompt; scores are ray-cast over the FOV sector (stopping at obstacles) and fused into a 2D value map, then smoothed with a 3x3 Gaussian and normalized to [0,1].

Target Prediction Module: U-Net-style multi-scale encoder (1x1 embedding) plus a GAP and FC coordinate decoder regressing target (x,y) from the multi-channel semantic map, trained with MSE; the output is turned into a Euclidean distance map.
Semantic Cue Intensity: fraction of FOV pixels with a non-empty label and confidence >0.6 in the multi-object maps; sets w_vlm=SCI and w_pred=1-SCI (dense >0.6, sparse <0.3).
Dual-model Aggregation Reasoning (DAR): DAR = w_pred/(D+eps) + w_vlm*V for each frontier point; the argmax is the next long-term goal.

Target locking: a target is locked when CMap_target>0.7; a fusion confidence map averages the single- and multi-object confidences on overlapping cells, and the max cell gives the goal, snapped to the nearest navigable explored point.
Waypoint navigation: A* global path; a waypoint 1 m ahead is passed to the iPlanner local planner.

setting.backbone: SmolVLM-500M (frozen) value map + GroundingDINO + Mobile-SAM (frozen) + U-Net target predictor (trained) + iPlanner local planner
setting.training_data: U-Net target prediction module trained on semantic maps with GT target coordinates (dataset and scale not specified); other models are pre-trained and used zero-shot
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D 640x480, 79° HFOV, camera height 0.88 m (plus pose for mapping)
setting.action_space: discrete: MOVE FORWARD 0.25 m, TURN LEFT/RIGHT 30°, STOP

numbers.backbone: SmolVLM-500M + U-Net target predictor + GroundingDINO + Mobile-SAM
numbers.extra: Target prediction module is trained (marked non-unsupervised); max 500 steps; run in Gazebo
numbers.evidence: Table 1: Comparison with previous work on MP3D: SONAR (Ours) 38.4 / 17.7

numbers_note: Only SR and SPL are reported. The MP3D val split is described as 11 scenes and 2,195 episodes, but evaluation in Gazebo may differ from the standard Habitat protocol. Baseline numbers appear to be copied from other papers.
results: SONAR reaches SR 38.4 and SPL 17.7 on MP3D, beating the strongest zero-shot baseline VLFM (36.4/17.5) and the supervised SemExp (36.0/14.4). Ablations show every component contributes, with the target prediction module the most important.
limitations: Gains over VLFM are small (SPL +0.2), and there is no variance or multi-seed reporting.
Evaluated only on MP3D in Gazebo with SR and SPL; no real-robot experiments, no other benchmarks, and the training data of the target predictor is unspecified.
SCI thresholds (0.6/0.3) and the linear weighting are heuristic and not ablated; the method is not truly zero-shot because it needs a trained predictor.
